Theorem
[Weak Harnack inequality] 1. ch8:8.18\group ch08-generalized-solutions Under the coefficient and data hypotheses of Theorem 8.17, let $u$ be a supersolution that is nonnegative in $B_{4R}(y)\subset \Omega $. For $1\leq p<n/(n-2)$, egin{equation} R^{-n/p}\| u\| _{L^p(B_{2R}(y))} \leq C\left(\inf _{B_R(y)}u+k(R) ight), ag {8.47} \end{equation} where $C=C(n,\Lambda /\lambda , u R,q,p)$.
Proof

\sketch Scale first to $R=1$, put $ ar u=u+k$, and use, for a cutoff $\eta $ and $ eta e 0$,

egin{equation} ag {8.48} v=\eta ^2 ar u^ eta , \end{equation}

whose derivative is

egin{equation} ag {8.49} Dv=2\eta D\eta \, ar u^ eta + eta \eta ^2 ar u^{ eta -1}Du. \end{equation}

Substitution in the weak inequality gives

egin{equation} ag {8.50} eta \int \eta ^2 ar u^{ eta -1}Du\cdot A +2\int \eta D\eta \cdot A\, ar u^ eta -\int \eta ^2 ar u^ eta B\ egin{cases} \leq 0,& u ext{ subsolution},\ \geq 0,& u ext{ supersolution}. \end{cases} \end{equation}

For $0<\varepsilon \leq 1$, the structural terms satisfy

egin{equation} ag {8.51} |\eta D\eta \cdot A\, ar u^ eta | \leq rac\varepsilon 2\eta ^2 ar u^{ eta -1}|Du|^2 +\left(1+ rac{|a|^2}{2\varepsilon } ight)|D\eta |^2 ar u^{ eta +1} +b\eta ^2 ar u^{ eta +1}. \end{equation}

Taking $\varepsilon =\min (1,| eta |/4)$ yields

egin{equation} ag {8.52} \int \eta ^2 ar u^{ eta -1}|Du|^2 \leq C(| eta |)\int igl(b\eta ^2+(1+|a|^2)|D\eta |^2 igr) ar u^{ eta +1}. \end{equation}

With $\gamma = eta +1$ and $w= ar u^{\gamma /2}$ for $\gamma e 0$, while $w=\log ar u$ for $\gamma =0$, this becomes

egin{equation} ag {8.53} \int |\eta Dw|^2\leq egin{cases} C(| eta |)\gamma ^2\int (b\eta ^2+(1+|a|^2)|D\eta |^2)w^2,& \gamma e 0,\ C\int (b\eta ^2+(1+|a|^2)|D\eta |^2),& \gamma =0. \end{cases} \end{equation}

Sobolev, Hölder, and interpolation inequalities give

egin{equation} ag {8.54} \| \eta w\| _{2\widehat n/(\widehat n-2)} \leq C(1+|\gamma |)^{\sigma +1} \| (\eta +|D\eta |)w\| _2, \end{equation}

where $\sigma =\widehat n/(q-\widehat n)$. For cutoffs between $B_{r_1}$ and $B_{r_2}$,

egin{equation} ag {8.55} \| w\| _{2\chi ;B_{r_1}} \leq rac{C(1+|\gamma |)^{\sigma +1}}{r_2-r_1} \| w\| _{2;B_{r_2}}, \qquad \chi = rac{\widehat n}{\widehat n-2}. \end{equation}

Introduce

egin{equation} ag {8.56} \Phi (p,r)=\left(\int _{B_r}| ar u|^p\, dx ight)^{1/p}. \end{equation}

Then (8.55) is

egin{equation} ag {8.57} egin{aligned} \Phi (\chi \gamma ,r_1)& \leq \left( rac{C(1+|\gamma |)^{\sigma +1}}{r_2-r_1} ight)^{2/|\gamma |} \Phi (\gamma ,r_2),& & \gamma >0,\ \Phi (\gamma ,r_2)& \leq \left( rac{C(1+|\gamma |)^{\sigma +1}}{r_2-r_1} ight)^{2/|\gamma |} \Phi (\chi \gamma ,r_1),& & \gamma <0. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

Positive iteration gives

egin{equation} ag {8.58} \sup _{B_1} ar u\leq C\| ar u\| _{L^p(B_2)}, \end{equation}

while negative iteration gives, for $0<p_0<p<\chi $,

egin{equation} ag {8.59} \Phi (p,2)\leq C\Phi (p_0,3), \qquad \Phi (-p_0,3)\leq C\Phi (-\infty ,1). \end{equation}

It remains to bridge the moments:

egin{equation} ag {8.60} \Phi (p_0,3)\leq C\Phi (-p_0,3). \end{equation}

For $w=\log ar u$, the second line of (8.53) implies on every $B_{2r}\subset B_4$

egin{equation} ag {8.61} \int _{B_r}|Dw|\, dx\leq Cr^{n-1}. \end{equation}

John–Nirenberg gives (8.60). Rescale and let the auxiliary positive $k$ decrease to $k(R)$.
